subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: What Anthropic server-tool contract should OpenClaw support, and which defaults should govern opt-in, billing visibility, transcript replay, code execution, prompt tool calling, and allowed_callers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested feature crosses provider-owned execution, auth, session-state, and security boundaries where automation cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Design a plugin-owned opt-in contract
options.body: Support Anthropic native server tools through explicit provider/plugin configuration with security, billing, transcript replay, and allowed_callers rules defined before implementation.

options.title: Ship web search/fetch first
options.body: Limit the first phase to lower-risk native web search/fetch support and leave code_execution, prompt tool calling, and allowed_callers for a separate security-reviewed design.

options.title: Decline delegated execution for now
options.body: Keep Anthropic native server-side code execution and prompt tool calling out of OpenClaw until the provider execution and billing model has a stronger product commitment.

recommendation.title: Design a plugin-owned opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Support Anthropic native server tools through explicit provider/plugin configuration with security, billing, transcript replay, and allowed_callers rules defined before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is mainly a product/security contract choice across plugin/provider boundaries rather than a local transport parser repair.
